From 49584bb8ddbe8bcfc276c2d7dd3c8890f45f5970 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Waiman Long <longman@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Feb 2024 11:10:14 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] workqueue: Bind unbound workqueue rescuer to
 wq_unbound_cpumask

Commit 85f0ab43f9de ("kernel/workqueue: Bind rescuer to unbound
cpumask for WQ_UNBOUND") modified init_rescuer() to bind rescuer of
an unbound workqueue to the cpumask in wq->unbound_attrs. However
unbound_attrs->cpumask's of all workqueues are initialized to
cpu_possible_mask and will only be changed if it has the WQ_SYSFS flag
to expose a cpumask sysfs file to be written by users. So this patch
doesn't achieve what it is intended to do.

If an unbound workqueue is created after wq_unbound_cpumask is modified
and there is no more unbound cpumask update after that, the unbound
rescuer will be bound to all CPUs unless the workqueue is created
with the WQ_SYSFS flag and a user explicitly modified its cpumask
sysfs file.  Fix this problem by binding directly to wq_unbound_cpumask
in init_rescuer().

Fixes: 85f0ab43f9de ("kernel/workqueue: Bind rescuer to unbound cpumask for WQ_UNBOUND")
Signed-off-by: Waiman Long <longman@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>

diff --git a/kernel/workqueue.c b/kernel/workqueue.c
index a24c7cfb80b4..cd2c6edc5c66 100644
--- a/kernel/workqueue.c
+++ b/kernel/workqueue.c
@@ -5299,7 +5299,7 @@ static int init_rescuer(struct workqueue_struct *wq)
 
 	wq->rescuer = rescuer;
 	if (wq->flags & WQ_UNBOUND)
-		kthread_bind_mask(rescuer->task, wq->unbound_attrs->cpumask);
+		kthread_bind_mask(rescuer->task, wq_unbound_cpumask);
 	else
 		kthread_bind_mask(rescuer->task, cpu_possible_mask);
 	wake_up_process(rescuer->task);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/workqueue.c`**
- The line that binds the rescuer's task to the CPU mask has been modified. 
- The original code used `wq->unbound_attrs->cpumask` to bind the rescuer for unbound workqueues.
- The updated code now directly binds the rescuer to `wq_unbound_cpumask` instead.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (85f0ab43f9de) that incorrectly bound the rescuer of unbound workqueues to a potentially incorrect CPU mask. 
- By changing the binding to `wq_unbound_cpumask`, the patch ensures that the rescuer is correctly associated with the intended CPU mask, thus fixing the issue where unbound workqueues could inadvertently bind to all CPUs unless explicitly configured by the user.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
wq->unbound_attrs->cpumask = cpu_possible_mask;
if (wq->flags & WQ_UNBOUND)
    kthread_bind_mask(rescuer->task, wq->unbound_attrs->cpumask);
```
Reason:
The `unbound_attrs->cpumask` is initialized to `cpu_possible_mask` for all workqueues, which means that unless a workqueue is created with the `WQ_SYSFS` flag and the user modifies its cpumask, the rescuer for unbound workqueues will be bound to all CPUs. This behavior is unintended and leads to incorrect CPU binding for unbound workqueues created after modifications to `wq_unbound_cpumask`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
kthread_bind_mask(rescuer->task, wq_unbound_cpumask);
```
Reason:
This change directly binds the rescuer to `wq_unbound_cpumask`, ensuring that the rescuer is correctly bound to the intended CPU mask for unbound workqueues, regardless of whether the workqueue was created with the `WQ_SYSFS` flag or not. This aligns the behavior with the intended functionality of the unbound workqueue.
